transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-09
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 47m
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Product), Maya Ortiz (Lyra VP ML), Devon Price (Lyra Platform Eng), Hana Kim (Lyra Data Scientist), Alex Rivera (Lyra Security)

Summary (auto): quick walkthrough of the Model Catalog curation playbook, interpretation of benchmark heuristics, and how Redwood's compatibility matrix maps to Lyra's latency/cost constraints. Agreed to run a targeted bench using Lyra prompts and to share SOC2/security docs and a pilot SOW.

Topics: catalog curation, benchmark heuristic signals, kernel/hardware compatibility, routing fallbacks, private deployment constraints, cost/latency tradeoffs

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate the time. quick intros from Redwood side, i'm samira, AE, and then ethan's our solutions engineer, jordan on product.
[00:08] Maya: hi all, maya here, VP of ML at lyra. excited to see how your catalog picks up open models for retrieval-augmented stuff.
[00:14] Ethan: great, thanks maya. real quick agenda: walkthrough of curation playbook, show the bench heuristics sheet, and demo the compatibility matrix view in the console. then q+a, and we map next steps.
[00:23] Devon: sound good. main constraints on our side, we need sub-150ms p50 for short-form completions, and cost is material — we're optimizing for throughput at scale. also, must run in VPC, possible private deployment later.
[00:36] Samira: got it. we'll focus on models that trade off latency vs unit cost. also show how the runtime suggests quantized variants and routing fallbacks.
[00:45] [00:45] Ethan: starting the screen share — ok console, model catalog. notice we tag each model with fit signals: accuracy proxy, bench latency distribution, memory footprint, and kernel compatibility. those are heuristics we derive from our open-bench runs.
[01:02] Hana: quick question — how do you calculate the accuracy proxy? is that evals against public datasets or do you do prompt-level tests?
[01:09] Jordan: good question. it's a composite. we run a small eval harness on public and curated prompt clusters, then weigh that with bench-derived truncation degradation. it's intentionally conservative — we surface a confidence band rather than a single score.
[01:24] Alex: from security perspective, when you say "bench runs" what data leaves our environment? we need to know about prompt leakage and telemetry.
[01:31] Ethan: for hosted we run synthetic bench payloads; for dedicated private we can run everything inside your VPC and only bring back aggregate metrics. any raw prompts can be redacted or hashed depending on your policy. we also have an optional no-telemetry profile for pilot.
[01:47] Maya: good. devon, do we have a shortlist of tasks we want to test?
[01:51] Devon: yes, three flows: short completion for search snippets (<=128 tokens), multi-turn chat for customer support (avg 700 tokens), and an embedding-heavy semantic search baseline.
[02:03] Samira: perfect — that maps to three bench profiles in our sheet. i'll show you the bench heuristics now.
[02:10] [02:10] Ethan: opening bench-spreadsheet-lyra.csv — top columns: model id, variant, quantization, p50/p90/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, memory (GB), compatibility flag for kernels (cuda10/cuda11/llm-accel etc), and a quality delta vs baseline.
[02:27] Hana: i see some models labeled with weird names — are those internal tags? e.g., "mistral-lite-8k-q2" is that a community build?
[02:32] Ethan: yes, those are community builds or forks; we include a provenance column. naming can be messy — transcription sometimes shows different names.
[02:39] [02:39] Samira: one feature to note: the compatibility matrix in the console allows you to click a model and see recommended kernel variants per hardware profile, plus fallbacks. it will tell you, for example, if a model is better run on A100 with anum kernels or on T4 with quantized pathways.
[02:58] Devon: can that mapping be pinned per customer? we may want to force certain variants for compliance reasons.
[03:03] Jordan: yes, customers can pin model-version + kernel selection in private and dedicated modes. for hosted we default to cost-driven routing but you can set tiered policies.
[03:12] [03:12] Ethan: demo note — the console shows a compatibility heatmap. green = pass with native kernels, amber = needs quantization or different kernel, red = currently incompatible. click into a cell shows known issues and expected p99 delta.
[03:25] Maya: we care about p99 more than p90 for production. can your bench produce p99 under steady-state concurrency similar to our traffic?
[03:33] Ethan: yes, we can replay concurrency patterns. for the pilot we recommend an in-VPC bench with identical QPS and prompt mix — that gives realistic p99s and KV cache behavior.
[03:45] Alex: what about caching and prefix caching — do you preserve KV cache between calls for chat flows?
[03:50] Jordan: we maintain KV cache per session and have automatic prefix caching for common system prompts. small caveat: some quantized kernels have reduced kv retention which we note in the compatibility notes.
[04:04] [04:04] Hana: i noticed a "quality delta" column — what threshold do you use to recommend a fallback?
[04:10] Ethan: by default we mark fallback if the quality delta exceeds 3% on your chosen eval set or if latency improvement is >30% with acceptable quality drop. thresholds are customizable per customer.
[04:23] Devon: question on routing — can we set a cost cap so that routing will only pick variants under a per-token cost threshold?
[04:30] Samira: yes we have cost-aware routing policies. you can set absolute cents/token caps, or bucketed tiers (platinum/gold/silver) with fallback rules.
[04:40] Maya: okay interesting. can you show a quick example — pick a model and show the console path where it suggests quantization and the expected p99 improvement?
[04:46] [04:46] Ethan: sure, clicking into "open-llm-3b-finetune" — variant shows fp16 baseline on A100 p99=210ms, q4_0 on T4 p99=390ms but cost halves. compatibility notes: requires kernel patch for q4 which we've validated. predicted quality delta +1.8% (meaning slight regression). fallback policy suggests use A100 for p99-sensitive routes, T4 for background tasks.
[05:10] Hana: that predicted +1.8% — is that measured on Lyra's prompts or general?
[05:14] Ethan: general; for your pilot we'll run the same bench harness against your sample prompts and produce a Lyra-specific delta.
[05:21] [05:21] Maya: security note — we need KMS controls in private deployment and audit logs for token-level access. can you confirm those are available?
[05:28] Samira: yes, private deployments support customer-managed KMS/HSM, fine-grained audit logs, and RBAC. we also support SAML SSO and SCIM user sync.
[05:38] Alex: any compliance docs you can send now?
[05:41] Samira: i'll attach SOC2, data flow diagrams, and our private deployment checklist. will also include the bench spreadsheet with your prompt buckets.
[05:49] [05:49] Ethan: back to bench heuristics — another column we use is 'kernel fragility' which flags variants that are more likely to fail under large sequence lengths. we surface that so you don't pick a fragile q2 variant for long chat contexts.
[06:02] Devon: that is helpful — some of our chat sessions hit 4k tokens frequently. we need to ensure no silent truncation or KV corruption.
[06:10] Jordan: agreed. for long contexts we recommend models/kernels with verified KV integrity and we run long-seq soak tests for pilot.
[06:19] [06:19] Maya: can you talk about the automated picklist? we don't want to manually review 200 models. how do you prioritize?
[06:25] Ethan: the picklist is filter-driven: you set hard constraints (max p99, memory cap, region) and soft signals (quality, cost). the system scores and sorts models and recommends top 5-8 candidates per workload. you can promote/demote them and the picklist updates.
[06:41] Hana: does the system show provenance and license info for community models? we need license compliance checks.
[06:46] Jordan: yes, each model has a provenance + license disclosure. we flag models with ambiguous licenses for legal review.
[06:54] [06:54] Devon: for the pilot we prefer 2 shortlisted models per flow. what would you need from us to start?
[06:59] Samira: three things: 1) representative prompt files for the three flows, 2) network access/VPC egress constraints and infra contact, 3) success criteria (e.g., p99 <= X, cost <= Y per 1M tokens). once we have those ethan will run bench runs and return a bench report.
[07:18] Maya: we can get the prompts and infra details by end of week.
[07:22] Alex: security will need to review the private deployment checklist — i'll coordinate.
[07:26] [07:26] Ethan: one demo aside — the Optimize tab also suggests quantization profiles per workload and estimates the quality loss. it's conservative but useful to justify moving to q4 or q2.
[07:38] Hana: show the routing policy editor?
[07:40] Ethan: opening routing policies — you can add a policy: route by latency SLO, cost cap, region, and then the fallback chain. for example: primary = open-llm-3b@A100, fallback1 = open-llm-3b-q4@T4, fallback2 = smaller-2b@T4. each step shows expected p99 and unit cost.
[07:58] Devon: nice. are rollouts supported? we might want canary 5% traffic to a new variant.
[08:03] Jordan: absolutely — canary, A/B, and auto-rollback based on quality regression alerts tied to your eval prompts.
[08:11] [08:11] Maya: curious about multi-tenant isolation on dedicated — how do you guarantee no noisy neighbor effects?
[08:17] Samira: dedicated provides isolated GPU pools per account, configurable autoscale, and burst policies. we also expose token-level cost attribution so you can detect noisy neighbors early.
[08:29] Alex: do you provide SLA documents for dedicated?
[08:32] Samira: yes SLA for uptime and latency percentiles with enterprise contracts. i'll attach the SLA PDF.
[08:39] [08:39] Hana: small nit — i saw a note about "kernel heuristics for transformer blocks" in docs, can we get a pointer to the whitepaper?
[08:45] Ethan: i'll include the kernel heuristics whitepaper link in the follow-up.
[08:50] Devon: any third-party benchmarks we can reference for cost comparisons?
[08:54] Samira: we have an open-bench repo and some example runs vs public infra; i'll include that but we'll also provide Lyra-specific numbers after the in-VPC bench.
[09:03] [09:03] Maya: ok last question — if we decide to go private on-prem later, how painful is migration from hosted? data plane separation?
[09:11] Jordan: we designed it to be consistent — same API surface, model pinning and rollouts migrate. you'll need to port keys and set up private control plane; we provide migration playbooks and one of our infra engs helps with the lift.
[09:24] Alex: good — security will want to see the migration playbook.
[09:27] Samira: noted, will include migration playbook.
[09:31] [09:31] Ethan: to recap: we'll run a Lyra bench with your prompt buckets in-VPC, produce p50/p90/p99 and quality deltas, highlight kernel compatibility issues, and propose a picklist of 2 models per flow. we'll share SOC2/security docs and a pricing+pilot SOW.
[09:48] Maya: thanks, that works.
[09:51] Devon: timeline — can we aim to review the bench results by next Fri?
[09:55] Samira: yes that's feasible — ethan will run the bench mid-week if we get prompts and infra info by Wed.
[09:59] [09:59] Jordan: i'll create the routing policy examples and attach them.
[10:03] Samira: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the artifacts.
[10:07] Maya: thanks all. bye.

End of transcript.
